findings.what: The guard should be `n > 0`: with `n > 1`, the second line gets no newline and no indent, so it is glued onto the first line ("no flock at /tmp/xto set up..."), and only the third line onward is indented.

findings.quote: -        let written = "no flock at /tmp/x\n  to set up a flock there deliberately: mkdir -p /tmp/x";
findings.what: The emitter now adds the indent, but other callers that still write their own two-space indent after `\n` (as this test's message used to) will print four spaces unless every one of them was updated too.
